subject: [PrivDeploy] Integration mosaic: IaC hardening & CI gating review
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Li <bethany.li@acme.com>, ACME Systems <eng+infra@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Integration mosaic: IaC hardening & CI gating review

Hi Bethany / ACME infra team —

Per our SSO/network kickoff earlier this week, we pulled together a short review of the Terraform/Helm/Ansible surfaces that will touch ACME's air-gapped environment. Goal: identify any gating failures for compliance and agree on a small set of mitigations that keep your security team happy without blocking rollout.

High level asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the private repo hosting will allow signed module artifacts (GPG) and an internal OCI registry?
- Which subnets will allow outbound TLS to Redwood's control-plane for audit webhook delivery (we expect an egress-only, whitelisted flow)?
- Do you have constraints on helmPlugins / post-install hooks in the cluster that we should avoid?

I've attached a quick module-boundaries patch and a sanitized helm values file that show the recommended changes (nothing sensitive).

Next steps: internal review call Friday at 11am PT to walk the CI gating checklist and sign the evidence matrix. If you prefer, we can gap this into two shorter sessions (networking / artifact signing).

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: terraform-module-boundaries.patch (text)]
[Attachment: helm-values-sanitized.yaml (yaml)]

From: Bethany Li <bethany.li@acme.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Systems <eng+infra@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:03:15 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration mosaic: IaC hardening & CI gating review

Stephanie — thanks for the summary and the artifacts. Quick answers from our side before the call:

- We can host signed artifacts in our internal OCI registry (registry.acme.corp) and allow GPG-signed module tarballs. Policy team requires SHA256 and signature verification in CI.
- Egress: production clusters are strictly egress-controlled. We can open a CIDR range to the Redwood control plane for audit webhooks, but it must be documented in our change ticket and use mTLS.
- Helm hooks: policy forbids privileged post-install hooks. Any hook that creates hostPath mounts or system-level services will be redlined.

We'll have our security engineer (vendor-ops@secureops.io) on the call to confirm the evidence required. For the Friday slot, can we shift to 11:30am PT? We have a stand overlap.

— Bethany
Bethany Li
Principal Infra Engineer, ACME Systems
[Attachment: acme-artifact-policy.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Li <bethany.li@acme.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:22:40 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration mosaic: IaC hardening & CI gating review

Thanks Bethany — that's helpful. A few notes from our internal gating checklist attached:

- Terraform: we'll add a verification step in Redwood's module-publish pipeline to verify GPG signatures and compare SHA256. The attached patch suggests a shallow change to module metadata and a signing step in .github/workflows/publish.yml.
- Helm: we'll avoid any server-side hooks requiring elevated node permissions. Where we previously used post-install hooks for certificate bootstrap, propose replacing them with an init Job that runs as non-privileged user.
- Ansible: convert role-based playbooks into idempotent, namespaced roles; avoid package managers that require external internet access at runtime.

Irene — can you confirm the CI runner approach for air-gapped environments? If we need a local runner, we should list required packages and the minimum base image.

Attaching: ansible-playbook-roles.txt with recommended role map.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ansible-playbook-roles.txt (text)]

From: vendor-ops@secureops.io <vendor-ops@secureops.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Bethany Li <bethany.li@acme.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:47:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration mosaic: IaC hardening & CI gating review

Marissa/Bethany/Team —

Quick clarifications from the security ops review:
1) Evidence: for each release we need a signed artifact, a CI run ID with signature verification step, and a signed attestation (we accept a short SLSA statement).
2) Network: mTLS to the webhook endpoint + strict IP allowlist required. We prefer a mutual-auth cron that posts aggregated audit bundles once per hour rather than streaming every attempt.
3) Secrets: no plaintext secret injection during bootstrap. Use sealed-secrets or an internal KMS shim; provide a short threat model for the bootstrap flow.

We can provide a template attestation doc — attaching our preferred fields. If Redwood wants to operate a local runner, it must run at operator level 3 and be integrated with our internal job scheduler.

Regards,
SecureOps — Integration Team
[Attachment: secureops-attestation-template.docx (docx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Bethany Li <bethany.li@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, vendor-ops@secureops.io
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration mosaic: IaC hardening & CI gating review

Thanks everyone — good discussion. Agreed action items and owners:

- Redwood (Karthik / Irene): implement GPG verification step in module-publish pipeline; add SHA256 check. Timeline: branch PR by 2026-11-20.
- ACME (Bethany): confirm exact CIDR and upload mTLS cert thumbprints to HUBSPOT-ACME-98765. Timeline: 2026-11-18.
- SecureOps: provide attestation template (received) and a short checklist for run-level requirements (they'll fill in by 11/17).
- Marissa: update the helm-values-sanitized.yaml to replace post-install hooks with init jobs; share diff. Timeline: 2026-11-19.

I'll open a tracking ticket in our private board with the evidence matrix and link the Drive folder. If anything changes, ping the thread.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Deployments — Redwood Inference
